strategy.summary: Reproduce xsimd signed saturating-subtraction bug: ssub is implemented as sadd(x, -rhs); when rhs == numeric_limits<T>::min(), -rhs is not representable, so ssub wraps instead of saturating. Add the PR's test case '[xsimd api | ssub at type minimum]' to test/test_xsimd_api.cpp, build the xtest target, and observe CHECK_EQ failures on the buggy commit 90365b6b.

input_output_examples.input: batch<int32_t> on SSE2 (common kernel): ssub(1, INT_MIN)
extract(xsimd::ssub(B(value_type(0)), B(lo))) for signed value_type, lo = numeric_limits<value_type>::min()
input_output_examples.buggy_output: wraps; equals lo (e.g. -128 for int8_t, INT_MIN for int32_t) instead of hi

input_output_examples.input: extract(xsimd::ssub(B(value_type(1)), B(lo))) for signed value_type, lo = numeric_limits<value_type>::min()
input_output_examples.buggy_output: wraps; equals lo+1 (e.g. -127 for int8_t, INT_MIN+1 for int32_t) instead of hi

input_output_examples.input: extract(xsimd::ssub(B(value_type(5)), B(lo))) for unsigned value_type, lo = 0

C++ compiler: g++ 4.9+, clang 3.7+, or MSVC 2015 update 2+ (CI matrix.sys.compiler); set CXXFLAGS env var if needed.
Install cmake and (for the CI-style configure) ninja; also xtl and doctest test dependencies per environment.yml/test-environment.yml/CMakeLists.txt.

reproduction_steps: cd to repository root at buggy commit; confirm include/xsimd/arch/common/xsimd_common_arithmetic.hpp still implements signed ssub as sadd(x, -rhs).
Apply the test diff for test/test_xsimd_api.cpp (the '[xsimd api | ssub at type minimum]' TEST_CASE_TEMPLATE).
Configure and build with the CI-style cmake -GNinja configure plus ninja -C _build xtest.

strategy.test_command: ninja -C _build xtest  # then run the built xtest binary, optionally filtered with -tc="[xsimd api | ssub at type minimum]" (doctest)
strategy.expected_buggy_behavior: Signed-branch CHECK_EQ assertions fail: ssub(0, min) wraps back to min (int8_t: -128, not 127) and ssub(1, min) gives min+1 (int8_t: -127, not 127); same wrong wrap via the common kernel for batch<int32_t>/<int64_t> on x86 SSE/SSE2. Unsigned branch passes.
strategy.expected_fixed_behavior: Both signed assertions pass: ssub(B(0), B(min)) and ssub(B(1), B(min)) both saturate to numeric_limits<value_type>::max() (e.g. 127 for int8_t, INT_MAX for int32_t), and the unsigned branch returns 5.
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy commit 90365b6b the '[xsimd api | ssub at type minimum]' test FAILS (CHECK_EQ mismatch, wrapped negative value instead of max) for signed integral types; the same test PASSES at fixed commit 8ab55669.

strategy.summary: xsimd PR #1023 fixes complex pow accuracy by using xsimd::sincos; the buggy commit computes r*cos(theta) and r*sin(theta) separately. Reproduce by applying the PR's test/test_complex_power.cpp changes, building test_xsimd, and running the '[complex power]' selector; CHECK_EQ(diff, 0) fails on the buggy commit.

input_output_examples.input: For each batch i (i=0; i<nb_input; i+=size): detail::load_batch(lhs_in, lhs_np, i); detail::load_batch(rhs_in, rhs, i); out = pow(lhs_in, rhs_in); expected[i] = std::pow(l, r) scalar-wise; tol = std::numeric_limits<real_value_type>::epsilon().
input_output_examples.buggy_output: select(absa == ze, cplx_batch(ze), cplx_batch(r * cos(theta), r * sin(theta))) -> diff = detail::get_nb_diff_near(res, expected, epsilon) is nonzero, so CHECK_EQ(diff, 0) fails.
input_output_examples.expected_output: select(absa == ze, cplx_batch(ze), cplx_batch(r * sincosTheta.second, r * sincosTheta.first)) -> diff == 0, satisfying CHECK_EQ(diff, 0).
